item.title: Freshman phenom Tim Ibukunoluwa off to historic start for Siena
item.description: Siena's Tim Ibukunoluwa (13) drives past St. John's Reed Bailey (13) during the first half of an NCAA college basketball game Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, in the Queens borough of New York. (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II) (Frank Franklin II/Associated Press) ALBANY - Only six games into his college basketball career, Siena freshman Tim Ibukunoluwa is making Metro Conference history. He was named Metro Player and Rookie of the Week on Monday for the third time in as many weeks to begin the season. He's the first Metro freshman to win three Player of the Week honors in an entire season in the 47-year history of the league. "I kind of just try not to look at it," Ibukunoluwa said before practice. "I know what my goal is. My goal is to win every single game, win the Metro and get to the tournament. That (awards) stuff isn't really any of my goals, but obviously, it's nice for it to come with it. So I'm just looking at the wins." Siena fans will get to see the 6-foot-8 Australian phenom in person again when the Saints take on the University of Vermont at 7 p.m. Tuesday at MVP Arena. He's tied for fourth in the country at 25.2 points per game and ranks ninth at 10.5 rebounds per contest. In Saturday's 93-87 win at Bucknell , Ibukunoluwa finished with 34 points, 15 rebounds and six assists to become the first Division I freshman with at least 30 points, 15 rebounds and five assists in a game since the 1938-39 season, when the NCAA Tournament began, according to the data sites CBB Analytics and Stathead. He's the first Metro player in any class to win three straight Player of the Week awards since Iona's Nelly Junior Joseph won four in a row from Dec. 12, 2022 to Jan. 2, 2023. "He's been awesome with (the attention)," Siena coach Nevada Smith said. "He understands it. He's such a team-first guy. He just cares about winning and that's been his whole thing the whole time. He's just doing what it takes to help our team win and whatever comes to him is definitely well-deserved, but he's handled it really well." Ibukunoluwa also scored 16 points in last Wednesday's loss at St. John's. Red Storm coaching legend Rick Pitino said after that game that Ibukunoluwa has "great potential" and should stay at Siena as a sophomore to develop rather than transferring to a higher-level program for more money. Ibukunoluwa said he and his family haven't mapped out a long-term plan. "They just want the best for me and I want the best for myself," Ibukunoluwa said. "Just staying at a school that's going to have good development, that's going to push me and just to play somewhere I'm very comfortable and that I'm always trying to work and improve myself." Asked if he's worried about bigger schools trying to tamper with Ibukunoluwa, Smith replied, "Oh, for sure, they already try." "It's the worst thing about having a really good player at our level," Smith said. item.title: How weird vibes from the Springboks could have huge impact in Nations Championship final
item.description: To whatever extent the words of Rassie Erasmus were lost in translation last week, South Africa used their team announcement press conference on Monday to make a clear point. With Erasmus unable to conduct media duties under the terms of his ban from World Rugby , assistant coach Mzwandile Stick stood in at the Springboks ’ hotel in southwest London – taking questions in English but answering only in Xhosa, his first language. It was explained that the coaching staff wanted to ensure nothing was misinterpreted. With the dedicated Kuhle Sonkosi – a former lock who now works for South African broadcaster SuperSport – acting as an impromptu translator, Stick spent a slightly stilted half-an-hour explaining a heavily-changed team for the Nations Championship final against France. He espoused the virtues of Manu Tshituka, the Congo-born back rower compared to Pieter-Steph du Toit primed for an international debut at Twickenham on Sunday. Mzwandile Stick conducted his press briefing entirely in Xhosa (PA) At one point, Stick cracked a joke about his good looks being the reason he attracted more attention than other coaches from the cameras in Dublin, insisting that it had been a collective effort to replace Erasmus. To Sonkosi’s credit, the remark drew a chuckle even on translation. Clearly, the coach was entitled to converse in his mother tongue if he wished to; South Africa has 12 official languages, of course. As is generally the case, he was engaging company. Stick (left) stood in for Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus (Getty) Yet one could should not shake a slightly peculiar feel. In part, that has to do with a side going into a final, with two trophies potentially on the line, on the heels of consecutive defeats. “Obviously, it’s not ideal to go into the final having lost back-to-back losses,” Stick admitted. “I think the more we’re frustrated at is that we haven’t played to our standards. For us, it’s very important to stop this run.” A shot at revenge against France is welcome after a game of fine margins; the Springboks coach rightly noted that his side had come out on the right side of three one-point contests on their way to World Cup glory two years ago. But the weirdness pervaded beyond the oddities of this new competition. item.title: Jaime Jaquez Jr. Still Fits Miami Heat Culture Despite Trade
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The trade sent Jaime Jaquez Jr. to Milwaukee, yet the Miami Heat connection never truly broke. He returned to the Kaseya Center on November 18 wearing a Bucks jersey and played with the same grit Miami fans love. With the Heat securing a 137–130 victory, he tallied 10 points and dished out five assists to lead his team in that matchup. According to local reports from Ethan Skolnick, insiders and fans are already anticipating a potential reunion as soon as he becomes available. Jaquez has not lost his edge in his first 18 games with the Bucks. He is averaging 14.6 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 2.9 assists while shooting 42.5% from three-point range. Yahoo Sports notes that his performance has cemented the view that he personifies the traits characterizing “Heat culture.” This culture relies on physicality, downhill pressure, and a willingness to do the dirty work without needing special plays drawn up. Why The Heat Still Want Him Back Miami values players who fit their specific identity, and Jaquez fits it perfectly. His blue-collar mentality matches the ethos the franchise demands from every single player on the roster. Although the Bucks hold the reins on his restricted free agency and any extension discussions, the connection between his style and Miami’s requirements persists. The front office knows that a player who works hard and plays tough is exactly what they need to win again. Fans will keep watching his progress closely as the season unfolds. Should the trade market change, they seek an opportunity to bring him back to South Florida. His stats show he can score and defend, which are the two most important things for a Heat forward. A Look At The Current Roster The Heat are also finding their own rhythm with other young players. Nikola Jovic is carving out a role thanks to his defensive tenacity, though his shooting splits are still low at 32.4/25.0/78.6. Meanwhile, Davion Mitchell has become a key piece after joining in the Jimmy Butler trade. He is averaging 17 points and 8.6 assists while shooting 51% from the field. Mitchell’s ascent has aided the Heat throughout their ongoing seven-game winning streak. Dwyane Wade praised his work ethic on his YouTube channel, noting that Mitchell travels with a basketball everywhere he goes as a grown man. “A guy that walks around and travel with a basketball everywhere he goes as a grown man, I’m rocking with him,” said Wade. The Heat have a clear path forward with players who love the game and work hard. Whether Jaquez returns or not, the team has found a way to keep its core values alive. The roster is built on players who understand what it takes to succeed in Miami. Jaquez recorded 10 points and five assists in his return game on November 18.

item.title: Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana hits out at Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe critics and demands respect for 'killer' former PSG superstar
item.description: Kylian Mbappe - Getty Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has mounted a passionate defence of Kylian Mbappe's Ligue 1 record, insisting his international team-mate's achievements are far too often downplayed. The French centre-back also sparked debate by comparing Mbappe at his peak to Brazilian icon Neymar. Fofana leaps to defence of Mbappe's French legacy Fofana has passionately defended Mbappe's record in Ligue 1, arguing that the forward's achievements in France are frequently trivialised. Speaking as a guest on the YouTube show Zack en Roue Libre , the French centre-back insisted that critics fail to appreciate the true scale of Mbappe's dominance during his time in his homeland. Mbappe rose through the youth academy at Monaco before spending seven prolific years at PSG. Despite his extraordinary goalscoring output across those seasons, Fofana believes public perception has unfairly downplayed his domestic exploits. Chelsea star compares prime Mbappe to Neymar To illustrate Mbappe's brilliance, Fofana weighed the French superstar against his former PSG star Neymar, placing the Brazilian just behind football's two greatest modern icons. However, the Chelsea defender maintained that Mbappe's relentless efficiency in Ligue 1 matched Neymar's peak level. "If you take Mbappe in his prime and Neymar in his prime, it is a close contest," Fofana said. "Neymar is the ultimate player after CR7 and Messi. But what I saw from Mbappe in Ligue 1 was insane. We trivialise what he did far too much." A dominant seven-year spell in the French capital After bursting onto the scene with Monaco, Mbappe seven-year stint at PSG saw him deliver relentless consistency week after week in Ligue 1. Having faced the challenge of defending against top-level attackers himself, Fofana offered a player's perspective on how difficult it is to maintain that standard. By labelling Mbappe a "hitman", the Chelsea defender emphasised the ruthless predictability of his goalscoring rather than sheer spectacle. "Mbappe is a hitman; every weekend it's a goal," he noted. "With Neymar, there is the flair, the madness, because you tell yourself, 'imagine if he had been serious'." Debate continues over Mbappe's place among football's elite Fofana's candid assessment is sure to fuel ongoing debates among supporters regarding how Mbappe's years in France should be judged alongside his peers. What is certain is that Mbappe will continue his campaign with Real Madrid this season, with Los Blancos set to face PSV in the Champions League. Meanwhile, Fofana will look to help the Blues secure a victory as they travel to face Nottingham Forest in the Premier League this weekend.

item.description: Liverpool have set their sights on move for 17-year-old midfielder Liverpool Eye Abdellah Ouazane as Julian Ward Steps Up Florian Wirtz Support Plan Liverpool are advancing plans in the market again, with fresh attention turning towards Ajax teenager Abdellah Ouazane as the club shapes the next phase of its squad build under Andoni Iraola and Julian Ward. According to Anfield Watch, the thinking at Anfield is increasingly focused on depth behind Florian Wirtz, whose recent form has underlined both his importance and the need for smart cover. The original report states that Liverpool are “exploring moves to sign a back-up for the German international” and that the club are now “ramping up moves to sign a back-up for Wirtz in the January window”. IMAGO Florian Wirtz Form Driving Liverpool Planning There is a straightforward logic to this. Liverpool are pleased with Wirtz and the numbers support that stance. As reported, he “created 10 chances against Man United all by himself” and now has “four assists and six goals in his last nine starts for club and country”. Those returns offer a strong indication of why he remains central to the attacking structure. Internally, there appears to be an acceptance that elite talent still needs protection. The report says Ward and the recruitment staff “are well aware that Wirtz needs a deputy. Liverpool cannot rely on him alone.” That line feels important. Recruitment at top clubs is rarely about replacing quality already in the building, it is about insulating it, sustaining it and ensuring the level does not drop across a long season. Abdellah Ouazane Emerges on Liverpool Shortlist Among the names under consideration, Ouazane stands out. Anfield Watch reports that “the Moroccan attacking midfielder who plays for Ajax has also been looked at by the Reds and is a serious candidate.” For Liverpool, that profile makes immediate sense. Ouazane is described as a player with versatility and projection. He has operated from the left, though he is also characterised as “a traditional no.10” and someone who “has also been deployed as a no.8 at youth level”. That positional flexibility has become increasingly valuable in modern recruitment, especially for clubs looking to future-proof several roles with one signing. The background is compelling too. item.title: Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt demolish Australia as England level T20 series
item.description: England’s all-Welsh opening partnership of Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt annihilated Australia with a brutal display of power hitting to level the T20 series in style on the Gold Coast. The pair rained down 13 sixes on the Carrara Oval in a frenzied stand of 151 that saw them make a target of 185 look like child’s play, speeding to an eight-wicket thrashing with 6.5 overs unused. The silent partner of the England and Wales Cricket Board made itself known in no uncertain terms after a false start in Melbourne on Saturday, with Swansea-born Donald blitzing 85 in 32 balls and Salt – who traded Denbighshire for Barbados as a schoolboy – adding 58 off 30. It was a devastating display which left some nasty scars on a pieced-together Australia attack that performed impressively to go 1-0 ahead at the MCG. Nikhil Chaudhary was taken apart by Donald in the fifth over, leaking 26 runs, before left-armer Joel Davies suffered even more grievously at Salt’s hands. Phil Salt batting for England on the Gold Coast (Dave Hunt/AAPImage via AP) His second over disappeared for an excruciating 31, including four sixes, a boundary and three skittish wides as he tried to hide the ball from his tormentor. Donald was hurtling towards a century when he picked out the catcher at long-on but, having scored just 56 runs in his first four innings during an uncertain start to his international career, this was no time for regrets. Salt also fell before the end, courtesy of a brilliant one-handed caught-and-bowled by Ben Dwarshuis, but their bullying partnership meant that was little more than damage-limitation. Tom Banton finished it off from the first ball of the 13th over, clearing the ropes for the third time in his own eight-ball cameo to end Australia’s pain. Despite the dominant nature of the chase, Australia would have been relatively content at the changeover, carving out 184 for eight on an unpredictable drop-in pitch. It turned out to be nowhere near enough but, after nailing 50 off the last three overs and watching Ben Dwarshuis end the innings with three consecutive sixes off Sam Curran , they had made their charge. England began by handing a debut to James Coles, who was immediately tasked with the first over of the day. He settled quickly by allowing just five singles, but that was a calm moment in an otherwise manic powerplay, during which Australia swung their way to 58 at the cost of four wickets. item.title: “Your Job to Create That Environment”: Fans Blame Lane Kiffin as He Criticizes Players for Playing for Themselves Ahead of Bowl Games
item.description: Louisiana State Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin. © Reuters LSU’s chances of making the college football playoffs are done and dusted, and with pressure on Lane Kiffin to justify the huge price tag that came with his appointment, the head coach would want his team to end on a high with the bowl games coming up. But Kiffin believes that players are only playing for themselves in the NIL era, pointing out the challenges that come with this generation. “They’re going to play for themselves and so if they put out bad film, they make bad decisions, they don’t hustle on a play, or they don’t play well, they’re hurting themselves whether that’s here or whether that’s somewhere else next year when they go to negotiate,” he said. Kiffin’s comments weren’t necessarily echoed by fans, with one saying, “He’s going to need a lot of talent to win with this attitude, it’s your job to create that environment in this landscape of college football it’s not easy for reasons he stated but you got to find that or LSU is going to have a budget bigger than anyone else and by a good margin.” Lane Kiffin Apologized for Using Profanity in a Halftime Interview Lane Kiffin recently used some foul language at halftime on LSU’s radio network during the game against Tennessee, and was quick to apologize for his comments after LSU’s safety Ty Benefield was ejected for targeting. “I want to apologize for my language at halftime in the interview,” Kiffin said to reporters. “No excuses. I was frustrated with the first half and really couldn’t even hear the question, kind of like our center down in the student section. But there’s no reason for that. And so, to people who were offended, I apologize for that.” Kiffin also pointed out one core issue he wants to address with this LSU team. “I keep saying, ‘I’m not concerned about the future of the program. I’m excited about the future of the program, but we have one core issue to fix, and that’s how we finish games. We’re in these games against really, really good teams, and we don’t play well late, and that can be part of a mindset that we don’t have right.” LSU plays Arkansas this Saturday in Fayetteville. item.title: Roma eyeing Sporting Lisbon forward Fotis Ioannidis
item.description: Roma eyeing Sporting Lisbon forward Fotis Ioannidis Roma continues to monitor the attacking market ahead of the winter transfer window, evaluating various opportunities to strengthen Gian Piero Gasperini’s attack. Following rumors of interest in Endrick, another name has emerged that could fuel competition with AC Milan: Fotis Ioannidis, a 2000-born Greek striker currently playing for Sporting CP. AC Milan is closely monitoring Ioannidis in their search for a centre-forward to replace Camarda, including the Greek among the options being evaluated along with Endrick and Tresoldi. One potential player who could influence AC Milan’s interest is Ruben Amorim, who has previously worked with the striker at Sporting CP and knows his characteristics. According to Gianluca Di Marzio, Roma considers the player an interesting prospect, although they haven’t identified him as a top priority. The European calendar will soon offer the Giallorossi the opportunity to observe the striker firsthand. On December 8th, Ioannidis will face Roma in the Champions League for Sporting CP, a match that could be an important opportunity to assess his qualities. So far, the Greek has made 15 appearances this season, scoring two goals and providing two assists. Gasperini, however, is primarily looking for a winger with acceleration, the ability to beat his man, and the ability to attack space—characteristics different from those of a central striker like the Greek. Therefore, any further exploration of Ioannidis will also depend on the opportunities that arise during the January transfer window.

item.title: Real Madrid superstar coming to terms with his new reality at the club – report
item.description: Real Madrid superstar coming to terms with his new reality at the club – report Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has confirmed that Vinicius Jr. will start tonight against PSV Eindhoven, but the past month has done a lot of damage to the player’s status at the club. Serving a long suspension from La Liga for a red card he picked up against Villarreal, the Brazilian star slowly saw his place being taken over by Yan Diomande, whom the manager slowly began viewing as an option on the left flank. With the team’s results also improving after the forced change, it slowly began to become clear that Vinicius was no longer as irreplaceable as he had been over the years. For the first time in years, his place in the starting XI began being called into question. Phase of acceptance As reported by Radio Estadio Noche in a recent update, Vinicius is beginning to come to terms with the new reality around his situation. Diomande is slowly replacing Vinicius. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) He accepts that he is no longer an undisputed starter for Real Madrid, and that he can now be replaced in the dynamics. Needless to say, that requires a massive shift in mentality and a real sense of maturity for a player who has been the face of the club for years. With the acceptance of his situation, Vinicius also now understands that he may have to sit on the bench and watch Diomande as a starter for Real Madrid. Regardless of how mature his understanding may be, it will undoubtedly prick the player to see his spot being owned by a teammate. A hope for resurgence Vinicius had a great international break. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) For a long time, Vinicius’ situation this season seemed hopeless and his arc appeared to only be moving downhill. The recent international break, however, provided a sense of hope for the first time and handed the player a major confidence boost. In Brazil’s two games in the recent hiatus, Vinicius scored five goals including a hat-trick and a brace, putting aside his poor form and rediscovering his goalscoring boots. He started on the bench at the weekend, but his cameo was powerful and even played a critical part in Real Madrid’s comeback. As he prepares to start tonight, the player will be aware that a lot rides on what he makes of the opportunity . After all, he is already treading on a tightrope and is a couple of poor performances from definitely losing his starting spot.

There’s nothing like a little canapé to tempt the palate, and four goals at the Stadio Ennio Tardini are just that: a great way of sharpening the appetite before a meeting of the heavyweights. With Donyell Malen achieving AS Roma’s first four-goal Serie A appearance since Vincenzo Montella in 2002 – and let’s not forget Rodrigo Mora’s stunning 71’ cherry on top of the cake – there’s a huge amount of momentum under the team’s feet. Now, the Giallorossi carry that momentum to the Parc des Princes on Wednesday for a pivotal Matchday 5 UEFA Champions League clash against two-time defending champions (and daunting foe) Paris Saint-Germain. While Luis Enrique faces his former club amid a 12-match winning streak across all competitions, PSG’s attack has been rocked by consecutive ACL ruptures to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Désiré Doué . There’s a clear opening, and a huge amount of wind in the sails. So, is this the best time to strike? item.title: Sean McVay says he’s ‘excited’ about Rams after season-ending injury to Puka Nacua
item.description: Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are losing their star receiver for the season, but head coach Sean McVay is still excited for one key reason. The Los Angeles Rams are currently sitting at 6-4 in a tough division with the rampaging San Francisco 49ers and the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks. The team has had their share of injury issues pop up, most notably to star receiver Puka Nacua. In seven games this season, Nacua was averaging 10 receptions and just over 100 receiving yards per game. Nacua was initially diagnosed with multiple ligament sprains and turf toe after being injured on LA’s final offensive snap in Week 9 against the Commanders. Since then, it has been revealed that he will undergo MCL surgery and miss the rest of the season. Head coach Sean McVay is still ‘excited’. Sean McVay says he is ‘excited’ to see how the LA Rams respond to adversity and how other players step up Nacua being out isn’t the only concern plaguing McVay at the minute. Davante Adams has been out injured, and now even tight end Terrance Ferguson is set to undergo season-ending surgery. Their receiving options are looking extremely light at the minute, but McVay seems to have belief in his guys. Asked about the situation by The Athletic’s Nate Atkins, the head coach gave a surprising answer sharing his positive outlook regarding the remainder of the season. “Based on last week, I’m excited about what those guys that did get opportunities did,” McVay said. “Let’s continue to see if we can grow and figure out what it looks like. You know the information that I had at the time, but I don’t want it to ever be misunderstood. “I am confident in Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield and Xavier Smith and C.J. Daniels, and (Brennan) Presley getting a chance to get back there and return kicks. It’s a bummer to lose those two significant pieces, but I think you have to adjust and adapt. “This is the hand that we’re dealt. I’m excited about trying to watch these guys go shine and do everything we can with our decision-making and our thought process to help bring that to life collectively for our group. A lot of that stuff, there have been some moving parts. “The Terrance Ferguson stuff I just found out 30 minutes ago. The Puka stuff was, you gather more information and you decide on getting that surgery. There has been a flexibility that’s been necessary. We’ll look forward to hopefully getting Davante (Adams) back at some point too.” The Rams have won four games in a row and have been rolling. McVay is known for being a great motivator, and it seems he is relishing the challenge of finding ways to win even while missing some key pieces. It is going to be a tough season for the Rams, but at least their HC isn’t throwing in the towel. item.title: Barcelona ready to file criminal complaint against Real Madrid president Florentino Perez over Negreira statements
item.description: Barcelona ready to file criminal complaint against Real Madrid president Florentino Perez over Negreira statements Barcelona are preparing to escalate their legal dispute with Real Madrid president Florentino Perez, with SPORT reporting that the club could file a criminal complaint against him for defamation if he refuses to withdraw his accusations against the Catalan side. As per the outlet, the two parties are scheduled to attend a conciliation hearing in Madrid on Wednesday, November 25. However, Perez is not expected to appear in person and will instead send a lawyer, who will maintain his position on the disputed comments. The hearing is set to be a significant moment in the growing institutional conflict between Barcelona and Real Madrid, with the possibility of criminal proceedings now moving closer. Barcelona await Perez’s response at the conciliation hearing The purpose of Wednesday’s meeting is to give Perez an opportunity to retract statements that Barcelona considers false and damaging to its reputation. If he refuses to do so, the club intends to proceed with a criminal complaint. The legal process began on June 12, when Barcelona, then managed by interim president Rafa Yuste, initiated proceedings following Perez’s public accusations . Barcelona and Florentino Perez are set for crucial legal confrontation over Negreira case. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE/AFP via Getty Images) The club subsequently received a November 25 hearing date from the court on September 23. For what it is worth, the conciliation meeting is a preliminary requirement before Barcelona can formally pursue a criminal complaint for alleged calumnia under Article 205 of Spain’s Penal Code. Perez is not legally required to attend personally and can be represented. Negreira case comments behind Barcelona’s legal action The dispute stems from Perez’s press conference on May 12 and an interview the following day, during which he made accusations concerning Barcelona’s alleged relationship with referees and the Negreira case. Barcelona considers those remarks defamatory and argues that they have damaged the club’s public image. Explaining its position when the legal action was initiated, the club stated, “The purpose of this lawsuit is for Mr. Perez to retract certain statements he made knowingly falsehood and that are slanderous and offensive to the Club’s image and reputation.” The club is also seeking specific answers from the Real Madrid president. Florentino Perez could face legal action from Barcelona over Negreira case comments. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Their legal demands ask Perez to acknowledge his statements and either correct them or identify the referees he referred to as the “Negreira Boys”. Barcelona further wants him to specify the matches and incidents in which he believes alleged corruption took place. Florentino Perez’s latest comments could deepen the conflict The dispute has not subsided in the months since Barcelona initiated legal proceedings.

item.title: Meet Aneurin Donald - the Welshman seizing England chance in Australia
item.description: Aneurin Donald has played for Glamorgan, Hampshire and - currently - Derbyshire [Getty] From Gorseinon cricket club in Swansea to some of the most famous grounds in Australia. That is the journey England's latest Welsh batter Aneurin Donald is preparing to complete when the T20 five-match series starts against Australia on Saturday. Donald made his England debut in the home three-match series against Sri Lanka but this tour represents a step up. It is 12,000 miles between the Swansea suburb and the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) where the first game is being played. It is a journey that has taken many years since starting at his local cricket club. He originally came down with his father Andrew to watch the local rugby club but became hooked on cricket. "Gorseinon means so much to me," said Donald, speaking to the BBC at the Welfare Ground, where the two clubs are based. "My family and friends are so involved down here and I spent so much time there growing up as a kid, playing rugby and cricket. "I try and get back there as much as I can. It's the lifeblood of the community and the reason I got the chances I did. "The basis that I gathered here, the time and energy I spent training in the winter got me on the rung to professional sport and now an international cap." England's Donald ready to savour Welsh homecoming The Gorseinon work ethic and Leigh Halfpenny effect The one-lane indoor net, now called the Alan Jones indoor cricket centre after Gorseinon’s other England batter, helped shape Donald’s talent. "That one little indoor net lane we had is probably the big reason as to why I've made it as far as I have," said Donald. "It was a little tin shed with probably a five-yard run-up where my brother [Gafyn] used to bowl into the middle of my bat. "It was a massive part of my career now." Those nets included training when others were relaxing. "If I had to put one thing down in my junior years and what separated me was probably coming down and training and being able to use that little indoor shed," he adds. "My dad installed a belief in me if I was training on a day nobody else is, you have added that little extra, whatever time of year. "We used to go down every week and I can remember training on Christmas Eve. "It was freezing cold and I remember being wrapped up in scarves and there was ice on our breath." While the Donalds were freezing inside, outside honing his kicking skills was a Wales rugby icon who also started his sporting journey at Gorseinon. "We used to see Leigh Halfpenny kicking for hours on end and it's probably a reminder that work ethic is what makes great players like him great," said Donald. "I can’t compare my career with his but I took inspiration from seeing him out there." item.title: Bayern Munich in talks with Jamal Musiala after turbulent week
item.description: Bayern Munich in talks with Jamal Musiala after turbulent week This has been a turbulent week for Bayern Munich. The Bavarian giants drew 1-1 against FC Koln at the Allianz Arena, but more than the results, they suffered tremendous blows. Michael Olise and Harry Kane both got injured, with the England striker set to be out of action for almost three-to-four months. However, it is the situation with Jamal Musiala that has caused huge attention among all football fans across the world. Jamal Musiala: The current scenario (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) While injuries to Olise and Kane have added to Bayern’s growing concerns, the uncertainty surrounding Musiala has opened an altogether different and far more delicate chapter for the club. The 23-year-old has endured a frustrating spell on the sidelines, with recurring absence seizures and the medical treatment required to manage his neurological condition raising questions about when he can return to his best. The issue has also spilled into the public domain, with several prominent figures at Bayern weighing in on how the club should approach the situation. Christian Falk has now shed further light on developments in an article for Bild , and he kindly shared the full picture with CFBayern Insider . The debate gathered pace 16 days ago when honorary president Uli Hoeneß, 74, questioned Musiala’s salary during an appearance on the BR programme Sonntags-Stammtisch . CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen, 59, later addressed the matter, but the discussion intensified on Friday when Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, 71, called for Bayern to hold talks with the player’s representatives about a possible adjustment to his contract or wages if his recurring seizures and ongoing treatment prevent him from consistently rediscovering his previous level. Those conversations have now moved beyond public statements and into the boardroom. BILD spotted Musiala’s agents, Christian Schmid and Tobias Altschäffl of 11WINS, arriving at Bayern’s administrative offices at Säbener Straße at 11:06am on Tuesday for a meeting that had been kept under wraps. The groundwork for the summit had already been laid internally. Bayern’s supervisory board discussed Musiala’s circumstances last Monday, following his second spell of absence within 12 weeks, although the club’s senior figures had not previously sat down with his representatives to discuss their concerns and expectations directly. Communication between the two camps has nevertheless remained regular since the illness first emerged, with the agency keeping Bayern informed about medical assessments and periods when the player has been unavailable. Until now, most of that dialogue has involved sporting directors Max Eberl and Christoph Freund, alongside head coach Vincent Kompany. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
